what: Tools with no static one-hop inbound link from any sibling tool. Read by `node platform/pages/siblings.mjs --check` and by siblings.test.mjs. A ratchet, not a target: LOWER it in the same commit that closes a pair, so a new tool shipping with no sibling link turns a run red instead of waiting to be noticed. Raising it is a deliberate act that belongs in a pull request body with a reason.
why:
Measured 197 tools, 164 of them reachable from another tool only by walking back up to a category index. The related-tool strip rotates alphabetically inside a subcategory, so on a large subcategory a pair may never appear on each other's page. Fifteen commits between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-07 each closed exactly one such pair, every one found by a session happening to notice it -- two of them (#3718, #3723) landed while this tool was being written, and #3723 closed the asphalt pave/sealcoat pair the first report named. That is the argument for the tool rather than against it: the work was already being done, one pair at a time, off a worklist nobody had.

A budget of 0 means the next tool that ships without an inbound sibling link turns a run red on the day it lands rather than joining a worklist. Raising it again is still allowed and still belongs in a PR body with a reason -- a genuinely new vertical with no honest partner is a real reason, as the ats-resume-checker and certified-payroll-calculator entries above record. Fabricating a pairing to hold the number at 0 is not.
